about: A fictional day (a 2 am wake, then 6:47 am to 10:05 pm) as heard by the wristband of Margaret, 78, who lives alone with early memory problems; every person, place and call in it is invented.

flag_notes.scam: 15:02:03-15:05:17: caller posing as the bank's 'security department': account compromised, buy $500 of gift cards, read the numbers, within the hour, don't tell family. She asked 'which card do you need?' (15:03:50) but then said her daughter handles her money and hung up (15:05:01, 15:05:17). No cards bought. At 17:14:50-17:15:04 she started to tell Lisa ('a man rang') but said she didn't remember.
flag_notes.distress: No sustained distress. The brief fright after the near-fall (20:52:31, 20:52:45) and the 2 am disorientation (02:04:02) are covered by other flags. The TV drama lines 20:33:10-20:33:24 ('I can't breathe', 'call an ambulance', 'Mom, wake up') are broadcast speech and must NOT raise distress.
flag_notes.fall: Near-fall, no injury: the bath mat slid at 20:52:22, she caught the rail (20:52:12) and said nothing hurts (20:52:45).
flag_notes.medication: Morning pills clearly taken at 08:00-08:02. Evening pills uncertain: compartment open and empty, she does not remember taking them and chose not to double up (20:23:44-20:25:05). Metformin is out of refills (10:42:55).

needs_yes: Right knee pain going up the stairs, mentioned three times (07:39:48, 13:29:52, 17:13:18; also 13:30:01 "worse in the afternoon", 17:13:26). Lisa suggested a brace or cane (17:13:42); she refused a cane (17:13:49). Candidate HSA product: knee brace / support sleeve.
Dizziness / lightheadedness on standing up from a chair, "lately" (12:32:16, 12:32:24, 12:32:50, 12:33:25). For the doctor more than a product.
Bathroom safety: the bath mat slid and she nearly fell (20:52:22); a non-slip mat / grab bar is a reasonable suggestion (she voiced the problem, not a request).
needs_no: Cold hands (09:46:38 "always cold this time of year", 09:46:46 "it's nothing") - passing remark, not enough to recommend gloves or warmers.
Breathing problems or collapse - only in the TV drama (20:33:10, 20:33:16), not her.
An injury from the near-fall - she said nothing hurts (20:52:45).
Sleep aid / insomnia product - the one night wake (02:03:12) is a memory/disorientation signal; she did not complain about sleep.
Back pain or any pain other than the knee - not mentioned.
A cane - she explicitly refused one (17:13:49).
Hearing or vision aids - she misplaced her glasses (08:16:02, 21:52:30) but did not report trouble seeing.
for_doctor: Morning metformin, lisinopril and donepezil taken at 08:00 (08:00:40, 08:00:58, 08:01:20, 08:02:05).
Evening dose uncertain: pill compartment open and empty, she does not remember taking it, did not double up (20:23:44, 20:23:52, 20:24:05, 20:24:52).
Dizziness / greying out on standing up from a chair, happening "lately" (12:32:16, 12:32:50, 12:33:25) - possibly orthostatic; she takes lisinopril and recently started donepezil.
Right knee pain on the stairs, three times through the day, worse in the afternoon (07:39:48, 13:29:52, 13:30:01, 17:13:18).
Near-fall in the bathroom at 20:52 (mat slid, caught the rail, no injury) (20:52:12, 20:52:22, 20:52:45).
2 am disorientation: thought she had to go to work as a teacher, reoriented herself and went back to bed (02:04:02, 02:05:46, 02:06:27).

Memory: asked what day it was at 09:14:50 and again at 10:13:05; glasses found in the bread box (08:23:52); told the county-fair pie story twice (09:44:20, 17:14:10); could not recall the afternoon call (17:15:04). Preserved: full pie-crust recipe from memory (09:42:05-09:43:40), detailed 1969 classroom story (09:49:58-09:50:33), crossword answer (08:41:00).
Metformin out of refills; pharmacy request sent to the office (10:42:55, 10:43:03, 11:36:20). Appointment Tuesday the 17th at 2:30 (11:35:27).
for_caregiver: Scam call at 15:02 (fake bank security, gift cards, "don't tell anyone, not even family"); she bought nothing and said Lisa handles her money (15:03:09, 15:04:13, 15:05:01). She did not clearly tell Lisa about it on the evening call (17:14:50, 17:15:04).
Evening pills uncertain - she plans to ask Lisa tomorrow (20:24:05, 20:25:05).
Near-fall in the bathroom: the bath mat slid, no injury (20:52:22, 20:52:45). The mat may need replacing with a non-slip one.
Knee pain on the stairs; Lisa suggested a brace, she refused a cane (13:29:52, 17:13:18, 17:13:42, 17:13:49).
Pharmacy: metformin out of refills, she will call Monday at 10; delivery offered Monday afternoon (10:42:55, 10:43:44, 10:44:00).
Dr. Patel Tuesday the 17th at 2:30, bring pill bottles; June is driving, pickup at 2 (11:35:27, 11:36:05, 16:22:40).
Night wake at 2 am thinking she had to get to work; went back to bed by herself (02:04:02, 02:06:55).
She was unsure whether Lisa comes Friday or Saturday, then remembered Saturday (18:45:00, 18:45:10).

Good moments: June visited for 40 minutes (09:38:40-10:19:52); Ethan told her about his goal (17:10:23); she recited her pie recipe from memory (09:42:05). Frank (June's husband) offered to put up storm windows Sunday (09:55:48).
